title: Venice + Rome + Sicily · Short City Stops + Ionian Coast — June 2027

packing: Real layers for Etna: the summit runs 20–30°F colder than the coast with strong sun — pack fleece, windbreakers and closed shoes for all four.
Water shoes: Isola Bella and Mazzarò are pebble beaches; Fontane Bianche is the sandy exception.
International Driving Permit: required alongside a U.S. license to drive in Italy — get both adults’ IDPs from AAA before departure.

itinerary.labelHtml:
Day by day

Venice 2 · Rome 2 · Sicily 8

One full city day each, then four Ortigia nights and four near Taormina.

days.heading: Pittsburgh → Venice
days.daycost: International allowance; exact four-seat ticket unknown.

facts.label: PTO
facts.valueHtml: Departure counts unless an evening schedule is verified

days.note: Depart Thu Jun 10. Book VCE inbound and CTA outbound as one international multi-city ticket. Reject any return that reaches Pittsburgh after Jun 23.

days.heading: Arrive in Venice; canals, pizza, early bed
days.daycost: Airport transport and food are in the trip allowance.

facts.label: Base
facts.valueHtml: Cannaregio / Santa Lucia side of the historic island

days.note: Transfer from VCE to the city, drop bags and take one short canal walk. No timed attraction after the red-eye. Choose a property with AC and a practical luggage route; confirm stairs and bridges before booking.

days.heading: Rialto early, Grand Canal boat, gelato lanes
days.feel: One full Venice day, no museum marathon
days.daycost: ACTV and casual food are already included in the cash allowance.

facts.label: Kid hook
facts.valueHtml: The waterbus is part of the adventure

days.note: Walk to Rialto while the lanes are quieter, use a Grand Canal vaporetto ride for the big view, and wander San Marco’s exterior before a long lunch/rest. Finish with a short golden-hour stroll. Palace and basilica interiors are optional substitutions, not extra obligations.

spots.name: Grand Canal, Rialto + small Venice lanes
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosFlickr

images.alt: The Grand Canal opening toward Santa Maria della Salute at sunset
images.captionTitle: The Grand Canal opening toward Santa Maria della Salute at sunset

spots.cost: Outdoor squares and lanes are free. Current ACTV 48h pass €35/person: €140 for four before any youth offers. Airport connections are extra. Paid basilica, palace and gondola visits are optional and unpriced.
spots.climate: Venice June climatology is roughly 61–77°F; humidity and showers are possible. No lagoon swimming; the boats here are transport, not a swim day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the public vaporetto as the boat experience; walk short loops with gelato breaks instead of buying a gondola tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A gondola only if all four actively want it; request the full current boat price before agreeing.
spots.restoHtml:
• Farini — bakery breakfasts and pizza slices; pick a plain topping at the counter.
  • Rossopomodoro, San Marco — official Venice menu includes classic pizzas; a practical sit-down fallback near the square. Check the current menu before the trip.
spots.altboxHtml:
• If crowded or rainy, make the Grand Canal ride the headline and skip the longer walking loop.
  • Do not add Murano/Burano to this one full day; protect the children’s energy for Rome.

days.heading: Venice → Rome by train
days.feel: Unpack, then one easy neighborhood evening
days.daycost: Rail allowance $180–$360 for four; exact train unknown.

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: About 3h34 on the current fastest Italo route; allow 5–6h door to door

days.note: Use Venezia Santa Lucia to central Rome; pick a sensible morning departure rather than sacrificing the final Venice night to an early alarm. Afternoon apartment rest, a simple pizza dinner and an optional short fountain walk. Do not reserve another major attraction today.

days.heading: A little ancient Rome, then fountains + pizza
days.feel: One main sight, then let the kids set the pace
days.daycost: Current basic admission: €18/adult; under-18 admission free, reservations and ID required.
days.note: Keep the Colosseum visit to about 90 minutes, with a short Forum glimpse only if everyone wants it. Rest at the apartment after lunch. Trevi is an optional after-dinner stop, not a second ticketed half-day. Rome gets one full sightseeing day and two evenings, then you leave.

spots.cost: Current basic Colosseum family admission €36 (two adults, under-18s free with required reservations/ID). Optional Trevi basin €8 for four at the current €2 fee; recheck 2027 access.
spots.climate: Rome June planning proxy: roughly 61–83°F. Midday heat can exceed the average; use AC breaks. No natural swimming scheduled in Rome.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the official basic ticket; save the arena and underground upgrade for a trip where everyone wants it.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A short private family guide instead of a full-day tour; quote before booking.
spots.restoHtml:
• Dar Poeta, Trastevere — Margherita, marinara and fries on the current menu.
  • Tonnarello, Trastevere — pasta and pizza; request simple sauce and check the current menu. Plan an early meal to avoid a long queue.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Skip the longest queue and return after an apartment break.
  • Use a grocery picnic or plain takeaway pizza if restaurant waiting is tiring.

days.heading: Rome → Catania; settle into Ortigia
days.feel: Cities done; the beach half begins
days.daycost: Domestic flight + airport access already itemized.

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: Allow 6–7h from Rome apartment to Ortigia, including flight, rental pickup and drive

days.note: Take a daytime FCO–CTA nonstop, collect an automatic car and drive about an hour to Ortigia. Pick up groceries and swim only if everyone has energy. This separately ticketed flight is eight nights before the international return; there is no same-day self-transfer.

days.heading: Ortigia: market, Duomo + sea decks
days.daycost: Est. $140 · market lunch, castle entry, dinner
days.note: Morning market and Duomo piazza while it’s cool, Borderi sandwiches for lunch, a sea-deck swim in the afternoon and the Maniace point for sunset.

spots.cost: The island, Duomo piazza, market and sea decks are free to wander. Castello Maniace is about $9 adults / under-18 free (closed Monday); a one-hour sea-cave boat runs about $22–28 per person — verify both prices for 2027.
spots.climate: About 64–83°F air; Ionian water near 73°F. Swim off the Ortigia sea decks or Cala Rossa in the calm morning, then retreat to shade or the apartment through the hottest early afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Build lunch from Caseificio Borderi sandwiches at the market and keep the sea decks and passeggiata as the free anchors.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the one-hour sea-cave boat from the marina on a calm morning and book a waterfront-adjacent apartment with AC and four real beds.
spots.restoHtml:
• Schiticchio — Ortigia’s go-to wood-fired pizza; plain Margherita on the menu
  • Caseificio Borderi — legendary market sandwiches made to order at lunch
  • Il Veliero — rustic family seafood spot with plain pasta for the kids
  • Keep breakfast fruit, granita stops and gelato in the daily plan — that is the local rhythm.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sea-deck swim + gelato loop when the day gets too hot for sights.
  • Aretusa spring + puppet museum for a low-output cultural hour.

days.heading: Greek Theatre + Noto golden hour
days.note: Be at Neapolis for opening before the heat, then rest at the apartment through midday and give Noto the late afternoon — granita at Caffè Sicilia, photos when the limestone glows.

spots.cost: Parco Neapolis (Greek Theatre) is about $15 adults / $8 reduced at the official park tariff. Noto and Marzamemi cost nothing to walk. In June the INDA festival dresses the ancient theatre in wooden staging and closes it mid-afternoon on performance days — check the 2027 calendar before picking the morning.
spots.climate: Noto’s stone streets radiate heat by midday. Do the theatre and Noto in the morning, take the beach or pool break in the afternoon, and save golden-hour photos for after 5pm when the limestone glows.
spots.saveHtml: Save Combine the theatre with free Noto strolling and a Fontane Bianche beach afternoon; skip paid add-ons entirely.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book evening INDA festival seats — a Greek tragedy at sunset in the original theatre is a once-in-a-childhood upgrade if the 2027 dates line up.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caffè Sicilia — Noto’s famous granita and pastry stop on the main corso
  • Marzamemi piazza trattorias — casual pasta and pizza tables on the fishing-village square
  • Pack water and snacks — the archaeological park has little shade and simple kiosks.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Fontane Bianche beach replaces the afternoon if the kids are templed-out.
  • Vendicari reserve boardwalk for flamingos and an easy nature hour in the cooler evening.

facts.label: Purpose

facts.label: PTO

days.note: A slow Marzamemi wander and piazza lunch, then Fontane Bianche’s shallow white-sand bay — or nothing but the sea decks if the family wants a true rest day. Anything lost to weather earlier lands here.

days.heading: Transfer north + Isola Bella
days.note: Pack up after breakfast, drive the autostrada north, drop bags at the Giardini Naxos base and spend the afternoon on Isola Bella’s famous pebble causeway.

days.heading: Etna summit day
days.feel: The volcano the kids will remember
days.daycost: Est. $380 · cable car + jeep, lunch, granita
days.note: Drive the south slope to Rifugio Sapienza, ride the cable car (and 4x4 if conditions allow) toward the summit craters, then decompress with Alcantara’s cold river or Zafferana granita on the way down.

spots.name: Mount Etna south slope
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · etnaFlickr

images.alt: Lava fountains lighting Etna’s summit at night
images.captionTitle: Lava fountains lighting Etna’s summit at night

images.captionTitle: An ash plume glowing pink over Etna at sunset

images.alt: Trails winding between Etna’s red summit craters
images.captionTitle: Trails winding between Etna’s red summit craters

spots.cost: From Rifugio Sapienza the cable car is about $59 adults / $33 child 5–10 round trip; cable car plus 4x4 jeep to ~2,900m is about $86 adults / $55 child at the March 2026 tariff — roughly $310 for this family. The Silvestri craters at the parking lot are free.
spots.climate: Expect 20–30°F colder than the coast, strong sun and loose ash. Bring real layers, closed shoes and sunglasses for everyone; the upper mountain closes on volcanic-activity or wind warnings, so treat the jeep stage as conditional.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride only the cable car — or just walk the free Silvestri craters — and picnic from the Ortigia market instead of the mountain cafeterias.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the 4x4 + guide stage to ~2,900m for the closest family-legal look at the summit craters, and cap the day with granita in Zafferana Etnea.
spots.restoHtml:
• Passopomo — farm-to-table trattoria and pizza on the Zafferana slope
  • Zafferana Etnea gelaterias — the granita-and-brioche stop on the way down.
  • Mountain cafeterias at Sapienza are basic; a packed lunch beats them.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Gole dell’Alcantara ($2 municipal stairs or $14/$10 botanical park) for a cold-river canyon hour on the drive back.
  • Silvestri craters only if wind or activity closes the upper mountain — still a real volcano day.

days.heading: Taormina town + theatre
days.daycost: Est. $220 · theatre, cable car, boat or dinner
days.note: Teatro Antico early with Etna framed in the arches, corso wandering and granita, then a Mazzarò swim or the coast boat before the one dress-up dinner of the trip.

spots.cost: Teatro Antico is about $15 adults / $8 reduced (open to ~19:45 daily). Isola Bella’s reserve entry is about $4.50, the town cable car $7 one-way / $11 round trip, and a two-hour coast boat with swim stops runs about $33–50 per person — all 2025/2026 tariffs to recheck.
spots.climate: About 61–77°F with sea water near 72–74°F. The pebble beaches need water shoes; mornings are calmer for the boat and the theatre is most photogenic (and coolest) right after opening or before close.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the cable car down to Mazzarò, swim the free public stretch beside Isola Bella and picnic on the beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the two-hour coast boat around Isola Bella’s grottoes, then a corso passeggiata dinner — Taormina is the trip’s one dress-up evening.
spots.restoHtml:
• Vecchia Taormina — wood-fired pizza just off the corso; plain pies and fries
  • Al Saraceno — terrace pizza with Etna views; breaded chicken for picky kids
  • La Bussola — Giardini Naxos waterfront pizzeria-grill near the base
  • Granita at a corso café counts as breakfast here — lean in.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Beach-only day at Mazzarò if the town crowds are heavy (mid-June is film-festival season).
  • Giardini Naxos promenade evening for a calmer, cheaper dinner than the corso.

days.heading: Final Ionian swim + Etna weather buffer
days.feel: A real holiday, with no packing until evening
days.daycost: Public beach free; lido or boat costs use the activity allowance.
days.note: Repeat a favorite beach or the pool; use this slot for Etna only if earlier conditions prevented it. Pack by evening. Check CTA and Etna notices before the flight home; an airport disruption may require an earlier switch to Palermo and a re-ticketed return.

days.heading: Catania → Pittsburgh
days.feel: Land Jun 23, before the family commitment
days.daycost: Protected international return in the multi-city allowance.

facts.label: Must land
facts.valueHtml: PIT Jun 23, even if late evening

facts.valueHtml: Naxos → CTA about one hour; add rental return and check-in time

Into Venice, home from Catania

International · $6,800–$9,000 allowance

Price PIT → VCE Jun 10 / CTA → PIT Jun 23 as one protected multi-city ticket for all four. This exact route has no verified family fare. Existing Catania and Rome snapshots on other dates are context only, not a quote for this plan.

Rome → Catania · Jun 15

Ryanair’s current route page advertises June 2027 fares from €32.99 one way and current flights around 1h20. This is a monthly floor, not four Jun 15 seats. Allow $450–$850 including baggage/seat reserve; compare the full ITA checkout too. The domestic flight is separate, with eight Sicily nights before the return.

Venice · Rome · Sicily

A train between cities; one car for Sicily

Venice → Rome · Jun 13

Italo’s official route page advertises from €29.90 and about 3h34. Four headline full-price fares start at €119.60 before discounts; no selected-date train has been verified. Budget $180–$360 and 5–6h door to door. Choose Venezia Santa Lucia rather than adding a mainland transfer.

Venice boats + airport

AVM/ACTV currently lists €35 per 48h pass (€140 for four at standard fare). Marco Polo airport links are excluded; the current airport bus is €10/person one way. These costs are in the city transport allowance, not extras to add twice.

Sicily · Jun 15–23

Collect and return the automatic at CTA. Ortigia → Naxos is about 1h45; Naxos → CTA about an hour. Rental coverage, fuel, parking and tolls are in the $750–$1,100 allowance. Keep the IDP and ZTL checks from the detailed Sicily plan.

Venice · Rome · Sicily

Heat breaks and flexible island days

One anchor per city day

Rome: short Colosseum morning, then AC and snacks. Venice: boat ride and short lanes, with no mandatory museum interior. June averages do not rule out a heatwave.

Venice access rules

The municipality has published a 2027 calendar that includes Jun 11–13, 8:30–16:30. Final exemptions, operating rules and payment details still need the later implementing acts. Do not assume the hotel exemption process is automatic; ask the property and use the official portal.

Etna + flight home

Retain the Sicily June moderate fire-disruption planning band of 5–10%; it is an inference, not a forecast. Watch daily alerts and CTA ash notices. Jun 22 is a weather buffer; a return-airport change must be confirmed and re-ticketed, not assumed.

Venice · Rome · Sicily

June 10–23, with Juneteenth in Sicily

Jun 10 is Thursday; Jun 18 is the observed Juneteenth Friday. Counting the unverified departure day, allow nine PTO days if your employer observes the holiday, or ten if it does not. A verified after-work departure could save one. Jun 23 evening arrival in Pittsburgh is acceptable; Jun 24–26 are full days at home. A week-later shift would fail that commitment.

The family lodging allocation is Venice $700–$1,040 + Rome $600–$820 + Ortigia $880–$1,240 + Naxos $920–$1,320 = $3,100–$4,420. These are allocations, not supplier offers. Resolve the route before the attractions

First: price the two anchors

One protected PIT–VCE / CTA–PIT ticket, then refundable AC stays with four beds. Reject next-day PIT arrivals even if cheaper.

Price all seats and baggage; choose humane departures. Put the rental only on the eight Sicily nights. Avoid any same-day unprotected airline handoff.

This route design responds to a limited appetite for Rome: one full sightseeing day rather than three. Venice supplies a very different kind of city experience, and Sicily remains the long, flexible part of the holiday. Four bases and two internal moves make it busier than Sicily–Rome; that is the price of including all three destinations.
